candidates.cover_letter:
Nyddja R. Emmanuel
Fort Lauderdale, FL

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Adolescent Services Manager position with AWA. With more than ten years of experience in child welfare, youth services, case management, and program operations, along with a Bachelor’s degree in Criminology, I bring extensive experience supporting youth and families while maintaining the structure, accountability, and consistency necessary for successful programs.

Throughout my career with ChildNet, I worked extensively with children, adolescents, and families involved in the child welfare system. My responsibilities included managing complex cases, coordinating services, completing and monitoring required documentation, conducting home visits, collaborating with caregivers and community providers, and ensuring compliance with agency and state requirements. I also regularly responded to changing circumstances and sensitive situations that required sound judgment, professionalism, and a calm, solutions focused approach.

My experience with HANDY further strengthened my background in youth program management and leadership. I supervised AmeriCorps members, participated in interviewing prospective candidates, coordinated youth programming, and supported workforce development initiatives. I also oversaw certification programming, including OSHA 30 and Florida Ready to Work, helping ensure youth had access to meaningful training and employment opportunities. Because the programs were grant funded, I was responsible for supporting program deliverables, tracking participation and outcomes, maintaining documentation, and helping ensure services remained aligned with program expectations.

I am particularly interested in this position because it combines several areas in which I have significant experience: youth engagement, staff leadership, program coordination, documentation, compliance, family collaboration, and creating structured environments where young people can succeed. I am comfortable setting expectations, providing guidance and feedback, managing competing priorities, and addressing challenges while maintaining appropriate professional boundaries with youth.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience in youth services, program operations, and team leadership to AWA and contribute to a safe, supportive, and consistent environment for adolescents and their families. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background aligns with the Adolescent Services Manager position.

Sincerely,
Nyddja R. Emmanuel

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Committee, 

I’m thrilled to apply for the Adolescent Services Manager position posted on your website. I bring a combination of experiences as an educator, administrator, and program manager, and am eager to bring the strong foundation of knowledge, skills, and practices I’ve built throughout these environments to this role.

Throughout my career working in inner city public schools, private schools and nonprofit administration, I’ve supported hundreds of young people in their academic, professional and personal journeys. In these seven years, I’ve learned that meaningful mentorship begins with meaningful relationships. By first understanding young peoples’ interests, strengths, and needs through authentic discussions and community-building activities, I create spaces where they feel known, connected, and better prepared to engage.  

Alongside these practices, I believe structure allows adolescents, and the teams who support them, to thrive. As a teacher, establishing routines while being flexible to the ongoing needs of my students and their families made for safe, collaborative, and inclusive learning environments. As an administrator, strong organizational systems, expectations, and feedback culture enables me to efficiently approach challenges, track progress, and support my colleagues to feel comfortable and confident in their work.   

What draws me to Adolescent Wellness Academy is its commitment to compassionate-driven support that helps adolescents grow. As a people-centered person, I desire to not just lead a program, but a space where adolescents encounter the love and care needed to build the emotional intelligence, joy, and interpersonal awareness necessary to lead fulfilled lives. 

I believe my experiences would translate well working with adolescents, families, and team members at the Adolescent Wellness Academy, and would be honored to have the opportunity to further discuss how my skills and values align with your mission. 

With thanks and sincerity,                                                                                                          Dana Mais

questionnaire.response:
I am currently working as a Case Manager at Broward Partnership for the Homeless, where I began my journey in human services in July 2025. This experience has been incredibly valuable and has allowed me to grow both professionally and personally while developing a deeper understanding of the needs of the individuals and families I serve.
When I began this position, I anticipated maintaining a caseload of approximately 30 clients, which I understood would allow me to provide each individual with the attention, advocacy, and support they deserve. However, my caseload has grown to approximately 50 clients. While I remain committed to serving my clients effectively, the increased workload has made it challenging to provide the level of individualized service I believe is essential to being an effective case manager.
I initially intended to supplement my income by working a second job, but the demands of my current caseload make that unrealistic. My current salary is approximately $45,000 annually, and I am seeking an opportunity that provides greater financial stability while allowing me to remain fully committed to a career in human services.
I am passionate about helping others and want to continue building my career in this field. I am looking for an organization where I can bring my experience, compassion, and dedication to the work while earning a salary that provides the financial stability necessary for me to focus fully on my professional responsibilities. My goal is to find a position where I can be fully engaged, give 100% to the individuals I serve, and continue growing as a human services professional.

Reason for Leaving:
questionnaire.response:
In my previous position, I served as a Residential Program Director with Sunrise Community, where I was responsible for overseeing two group homes and supervising a team of approximately 20 staff members. My salary was $45,000 yearly but was raised to $55,000 after 3 months. This role was highly rewarding and provided me with valuable experience supporting individuals with mental health and intellectual disabilities. I found the work especially meaningful because it allowed me to advocate for the individuals we served while ensuring they received appropriate care, support, and services.

During my tenure (July 2024-2025), one of the homes under my supervision was closed, and I was subsequently transferred to Miami to manage two additional residential homes. This transition presented several significant operational challenges, including the need to work directly on the staff floor while simultaneously fulfilling my managerial responsibilities. In addition, there were ongoing operational and compliance concerns within the homes that created potential liabilities.

I made every effort to address these concerns through the appropriate management channels and advocated for the necessary corrective actions. Unfortunately, when several of the issues remained unresolved despite my efforts to bring them to upper management's attention, I ultimately made the difficult decision to leave the organization.

Despite the circumstances surrounding my departure, I remain grateful for the experience and the opportunity to serve individuals with disabilities. The position strengthened my leadership, problem-solving, staff-management, advocacy, and crisis-management skills, all of which continue to shape my approach to working in human services.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy,

I stumbled upon your company website and believe it is an incredible provision for so many young ones.  I currently work part time as a substitute teacher who teaches and guides students in various subjects. One subject that comes up constantly (not on the curriculum) is why people are so different. 
  I help students not only in academic areas but emotional and psychological areas that sometimes makes them feel alone or like outcasts.
When I reviewed the work that goes on at AWA, I immediately wanted to apply and find a position.  AWA is exactly what Florida and the whole world needs.  
  I enjoy helping people at all times, but helping the youth and future of our world is my passion.
While this is not the typical cover letter, what I would like to add is that I am a professional who has worked in healthcare and the school system. My goal is to do all that I can for people with compassion, empathy and the respect they deserve.
 It would be an honor to be part of a company such as AWA which does just that.

Thank you for your time,
Marilyn Vega

I have worked in administrative, psychiatric dept assistant coordinator, ESOL paraprofessional and customer service positions that help me qualify for a variety of positions.

questionnaire.text: What makes you interested in joining Adolescent Wellness Academy?
questionnaire.response: What makes me interested in joining AWA is the reviews, the mission and the fact that more treatment centers like AWA are needed.  The youth of the world is hurting in so many ways and AWA like other professionals is doing something GREAT to help.

questionnaire.text: What experience do you have supporting adolescents, families, or individuals receiving behavioral health services?
questionnaire.response:
In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I waited for my son and daughter to be eligible for preK and kindergarten so I could return to work.   I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English.  During those 9 years I learned not only to help many Spanish speaking students learn English, but how to care for the ones who were emotionally distressed from various personal problems at home, I would accompany them to the social workers office and translate all the problems they were experiencing at home. I realized how much suffering and empathy was needed for my role.  I later left the position to care for my son who had a massive brain tumor and barely survived during the surgery.  As my son, progressed and I was forced to stay home.  I found work on line, which happened to be during COVID. 
   I recently went back to work part time as a Substitute teacher, and still find myself helping students of all ages with a variety of emotional issues.

questionnaire.text: Is there anything specific you would like our People & Culture team to consider when reviewing your application?
questionnaire.response: I would like my qualities to be considered carefully.  I believe treating others the way you want to be treated is critical in this life.  Everyday I use qualities such as patience, mildness, tolerance and love in what I do.  These qualities are not only essential in our personal lives at home with our families, but when dealing with all people, especially those battling illnesses and obstacles!

Dear Hiring Team,
I am applying for the part-time Mental Health Program Coordinator position. My work as a clinical assistant and my previous experience as a teacher’s assistant at a private school have lit a fire in me and reaffirmed my passion for working with children and adolescents. Therefore, I would relish the opportunity to help teens and families navigate AWA's virtual mental health program.
In my current role at Manifest Psychology, Inc., I speak with prospective and established patients, schedule appointments, verify health insurance, and help find referral options when our practice cannot meet their needs. I enjoy listening to people’s concerns and helping them take the next step toward their mental health and well-being. I also spend a great deal of my time assisting the clinical psychologist and owner of the practice with psychological evaluation reports by organizing and entering assessment scores and all of the results from the questionnaires, self-reports, and observer reports for her review. I then proofread the final report after the psychologist completes her evaluation and officially renders a diagnosis. This work requires attention to detail, clear communication, and a real understanding of the assessments. It also requires a deep reverence for the patients and their families, and for the weight that diagnosis carries.
Previously, when I worked at For the Love of Learning Private School, I supported children and adolescents, primarily middle- and high-school students. This is where I discovered how much I loved working with teens. The best part of my day, even amid the chaos, was connecting with my students and listening with an open heart to their troubles and concerns; I became their safe space and sounding board. They shone a light on my path and confirmed how much I want to work with teens. These students lit a fire inside me and gave me clarity of purpose.
Additionally, I am pursuing a bachelor’s degree in psychology at Southern New Hampshire University, with concentrations in Mental Health Counseling and Child and Adolescent Development. I will graduate by the end of 2027, and next fall I will apply to a PsyD program to follow my dream of becoming a clinical psychologist. I have a particular interest in supporting children and adolescents affected by trauma and anxiety, and helping families access appropriate services. I understand the boundaries of a non-clinical position and the importance of promptly bringing safety concerns to the clinical team.
In this Mental Health Program Coordinator role, I would bring bilingual (Spanish) communication skills, clinical office experience, and a caring, empathetic, attentive approach that aligns with AWA's focus on youth wellness. Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how I can support your team and the families you serve.

Kind regards,

Jessica DiBiasio

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Adolescent Mental Health Program Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology, direct experience supporting youth and adolescents in behavioral health and educational settings, and a professional background in creative direction, community engagement, and program development, I bring a unique combination of mental health knowledge, relationship-building, organization, and creativity to this role.

My passion for working with young people has been an important part of my professional journey. As a Youth Behavior Specialist with Children’s Home of Reading, I provided supervision, guidance, boundaries, and support to youth while helping plan and supervise structured activities. I was responsible for maintaining a safe environment and supporting young people through challenging situations with patience, flexibility, and integrity. I also have experience providing behavioral health support through therapeutic services and working directly with students in educational settings.

Earlier in my career, I served as a Truancy Case Manager with Carson Valley Children’s Aid, where I worked closely with youth and families to assess progress, develop and implement plans, provide referrals and supportive counseling, maintain communication with schools, and document case information. This experience strengthened my ability to coordinate services, communicate with multiple stakeholders, advocate for young people, and remain organized while managing sensitive situations.

My background in psychology, combined with my experience in youth services, has given me a strong foundation in behavioral health, crisis intervention, de-escalation, active listening, behavioral progress monitoring, and youth program management. I am also bilingual in English and Spanish, which allows me to communicate with and build relationships across diverse communities.

In addition to my behavioral health experience, I have spent many years working as a Visual Artist and Creative Director, collaborating with major organizations and developing community-centered projects. This work has strengthened my leadership, project management, communication, event planning, and problem-solving abilities. I believe creativity can be an important tool in engaging adolescents and creating programs where young people feel seen, supported, and encouraged to participate.

I am currently preparing for future graduate studies in Psychology and am eager to continue developing my career in adolescent mental health. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, compassion, organizational skills, and commitment to youth development to Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background and experience could contribute to your team and the adolescents you serve.

Sincerely,

Anhia Santana

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,
I am applying for the Recruiter position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am a full cycle recruiter at Nextaff, where I have spent more than two years filling medical and industrial roles, and I would like to bring that experience to a team whose hiring directly affects the care young people receive.
At Nextaff I carry roughly a dozen requisitions at a time and take each one from sourcing through a confirmed first day. That means sourcing through job boards, direct outreach, referrals and email campaigns, running phone screens against the same question set so candidates are comparable, coordinating interviews, and handling reference checks, background checks, offers and onboarding. When the franchise transitioned, I expanded my desk into medical staffing and began recruiting for clinical and support roles against license, credential and background-check requirements. I know that in a clinical setting a hire is not finished until the paperwork is, so I keep candidate records current in the ATS and stay on top of compliance documents so start dates do not slip.
Two things set me apart. First, I built and deployed my own AI-driven automations for repetitive sourcing and candidate follow-up, which shortened our time-to-fill and gave me more time for conversations with candidates and hiring managers. Second, I am a native speaker of both English and Spanish, and I recruit and screen in both, which widens the applicant pool for healthcare roles. I already work independently and fully remote on Eastern time, and I am comfortable owning a requisition load without close supervision.
I would welcome the chance to talk about how I can help Adolescent Wellness Academy hire well and quickly. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in a behavioral health leadership, clinical operations, or clinical management opportunity within your organization. With a PhD in Psychology, Master’s-level training in Psychology, MCAP/CAP credentials, and extensive experience in behavioral health, substance use treatment, clinical supervision, and program operations, I bring a combination of clinical knowledge, leadership experience, and operational expertise that allows me to effectively support both clients and multidisciplinary teams.

I currently serve as a Clinical Director with Recovery Unplugged, where I provide clinical leadership within a substance use and co-occurring mental health treatment environment serving clients across residential and outpatient levels of care. My responsibilities include supporting clinical programming, supervising and collaborating with treatment professionals, reviewing clinical documentation, monitoring treatment progress, addressing client needs, facilitating therapeutic programming, and helping maintain quality and continuity of care. My experience with clinical systems and documentation platforms, including KIPU and other behavioral health technologies, has strengthened my ability to manage clinical operations while maintaining attention to compliance, documentation, and patient-centered care.

Prior to my current role, I developed significant leadership experience within behavioral health and correctional settings, including supervisory responsibilities across multiple facilities and teams. Throughout my career, I have been entrusted with increasing levels of responsibility, progressing from direct-service substance abuse counseling into supervisory and leadership positions. I have experience conducting clinical and operational reviews, supporting staff development, coordinating services, addressing complex client needs, and maintaining program standards. My background has also required me to work effectively with individuals experiencing substance use disorders, mental health concerns, trauma-related challenges, and complex psychosocial circumstances.

My academic and professional background has provided me with a strong foundation in evidence-based behavioral health practices, clinical assessment, treatment planning, group facilitation, and organizational leadership. I approach leadership with a balance of accountability and compassion, recognizing that successful clinical programs depend not only on quality services for clients but also on strong communication, effective supervision, teamwork, and a culture that supports professional growth.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical experience, leadership background, and commitment to behavioral health to your organization. I am confident that my combination of direct clinical experience and executive-level operational perspective would allow me to contribute meaningfully to your team and the individuals you serve.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and qualifications can support your organization’s goals.

Sincerely,

Dr. Richild Morgan, PhD, MCAP

• Trauma-Informed Advocacy & Case Management: Over 15 years directly managing dependency cases, conducting judicial reviews, and advocating for children and families within the legal and child welfare systems.
• Cross-Sector Community Collaboration: Proven success building referral networks and partnering with healthcare providers, behavioral health specialists, court officers, and local social services.
• Mission-Driven Operational Leadership: Successfully led teams of 70+ resource coordination staff and Citizen Review Panels, maintaining high quality-assurance standards while ensuring members and families receive timely, dignified care.
In my recent leadership roles—including Resource Coordination Manager at Centene and CRP Program Manager at Florida Foster Care Review—I have focused on ensuring that system-level operations directly elevate client care. Whether facilitating Citizen Review Panel hearings for foster youth or overseeing large-scale care management teams connecting healthcare members to vital social and behavioral health resources, my goal remains unchanged: ensuring every individual is heard, supported, and connected to the services they need to thrive.
As a bilingual professional (English/Spanish) holding a degree in Psychology with a Sociology minor, I bring cultural competence, empathy, and proven leadership to your organization's social work initiatives. I am eager to discuss how my background in community advocacy, social service leadership, and case management operations can contribute to your mission. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,
Melissa E. Diaz
